utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 20th of February, in spite of all agreements and joint orders, the traffic between Kiseljak and Busovaca was not re-established, even for the humanitarian aid convoys. Can you tell us, what information did you receive on that day?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: On that day, I received information that new forces had been brought, that is, the forces of the BH army, were brought at Bilalovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Caritas was trying to reach Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that Caritas was trying to deliver food for the parish of Busovaca, I was informed of these incidents, and we also forwarded the information to the UNPROFOR headquarters in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 21st of February, 1993, new BH army checkpoints were set up in Smajlovici, Bukovci, Bilalovac. Can you comment on those?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: It is this checkpoint on the road to Fojnica. This was Smajlovici (indicating). It was set up, and I have to say that myself and the commander of the 3rd Corps, at the meeting in Kakanj, had drafted a joint order to remove all the checkpoints and barricades on the roads. This checkpoint was set up when the civilians were expelled from Busovaca and they were driven to Kiseljak, and they attempted to use that road to go back via Sebesic and reach Busovaca again. They were stopped at Smajlovici, at the checkpoint, and the checkpoint Oseliste-Bukovice was especially worrisome for us because it was also set up after the joint order was issued, and there was an anti-aircraft 20-millimetre calibre gun set up at that checkpoint, which was a rarity at that time to use anti-aircraft machine gun at the checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You just sat down, but if you can just again come to the model and point for the Trial Chamber where the positions, that is, the front lines between the army of BH and the HVO, were and to point how you placed the flags to mark that front line?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: I think that I can make it much more precisely on the map --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So why don't you first show it on the map and then we will move to the model?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: As of January 1993, the front line in Busovaca was as follows: I am pointing to the town of Busovaca due north, the Kuber range, the Saracevic feature 957, the village of Putis, Katici, via Bobovisce to Mejdani, Solakovici, that is Kula, Bilalice, Donje Polje, Prosje, Modri Kamen, Pridolci, Luske Staje, Busovacke Staje, Rog, Kovacevac, Rovna -- that is Donja Rovna. That was the line, and the forces were -- and now I'm moving to the forces in the village municipality. I'm pointing at Kiseljak town. This was the deployment: Pobrdze, Demici, Dugo Polje, Medovici, Dundjeri, and the village of Badnje. On the model, this is Busovaca (indicating), forces at Kuber, Saracevica, and feature 957, the village of Katici, then Kula, Milavice, Prosje, Modrikamen, Pridolci, Luske Staje does not appear on the model, Busovacke Staje does not appear on the model, the Rog feature, and further Donja Rovna.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: For the record, please, the green flags are the BH army line, and facing them, the blue flags are the HVO lines; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the territory of Kiseljak municipality, the forces were deployed along the lines of Pobrdze, Demici, then Dugo Polje, Dundjeri, Badnje, and the area from the Kacuni local commune to Bilalovac, and perhaps it would be better if I used paper here, I can use this small piece here. So this area was an area without any Croatian presence. Those who had stayed behind, the elderly people, like Grubesici, Ljoljo, and others, were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you say -- did no Croats live there or they were driven out of there, they were expelled, cleansed?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: I am talking about the Croats who were expelled during this conflict. This area of Dusina, Lasva, and Visnjica belonged to the Zenica municipality, and from these villages, Croats were also ethnically cleansed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Would you now sit down again, and while we're at ethnic cleansing, the joint commission --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Therefore, the joint commission for Busovaca, the HVO, and the BH army went all over the majority of this area, and they ascertained together figures on the destruction of Croatian houses, civilian property, and the Croatian casualties, so could you give the facts and figures of that joint commission?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: They are the figures which were not the final figures but were figures sent to us by the joint commission at a meeting held on the 21st of February, 1993, and all these figures --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. If there are figures coming from a document that has been sent by the joint commission, I would ask if the Court and Prosecution can see that documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we don't have that document. We don't have that document. All we have are the personal records and notes of Mr. Blaskic and his recollections, but we haven't got a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I share the opinion of Mr. Nobilo. The witness will tell you of the figures. He will say whether they were figures that he received officially or whether they were figures that he, himself, assessed. Where did the figures come from, Mr. Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, they are not my assessments. They are official findings by a joint commission composed of the European Monitors under the direct command of the head of the European Monitoring Mission for the Zenica region, and the meeting, at which I heard these figures from the joint commission and took note of this information, was under the organisation of the European Monitoring Mission, and present at the meeting were UN officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So can we clarify this matter? You were told this information orally at the meeting, were you not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: Yes, this information was reported to us by the joint commission, and Enver and myself, together with Mr. Flemming and Mr. Stewart, we accepted the report provided by the joint commission and set out at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: But the report was orally submitted, was it not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did not receive a written document from the joint commission, it was orally submitted, and probably the European Monitoring Mission compiled this document for its own purposes, for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Well, continue. According to the best of your recollections and your notes, what were the findings of the European Commission?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: The findings of the European Commission were as follows: A total of 548 families were expelled of the Croatian ethnicity, and the figure of 2.101 individuals, 2.101 individuals. From the village of Oseliste, 51 families, households, 273 individuals; from the village of Bukovci, the figures are as follows: 28 families, 103 individuals; the village of Gusti Grab, 57 families, 285 individuals; the village of Prosje, six families, 26 individuals; the village of Milavice, four families, 20 individuals; the village of Gornji Solakovici, 18 families, 85 individuals; the village of Nezirovici, 45 families, 131 individuals; the village of Kacuni, 53 families, 203 individuals; the Kiseljak municipality, 240 families; from the Bilalovac local community, 800 individuals; the municipality of Zenica, 46 families, 175 individuals; from the villages of Dusina, 12 families, 45 individuals; the village of Visnjica, 20 families, 80 individuals; the village of Lasva, 14 families, 50 individuals. Those were the findings of the joint commission of the 3rd Corps of the HVO of the European Monitoring Mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: At that meeting, did you take note of the fact that all the prisoners were released? Was that noted, if you can remember? If not, never mind.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: I don't remember whether that was taken, whether we were able to observe that at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Let us now move on to the 23rd of February when the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina brought to Gomionica some concrete blocks or devices. Can you tell us what they were, what that was all about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: They were facilities which were used by the former Yugoslav People's Army manufactured to type, and they were armoured concrete bunkers composed of various elements, prefabricated elements, that could be transported to different locations where they were built in as fortification for combat operations and for protection purposes, so they are the classical standard type of military bunkers offering high-grade protection and highly conducive to combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The Kiseljak-Busovaca road, 40 days from when it was blocked, was it free?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: No, the road was not deblocked. It remained blocked to members of the HVO and the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 25th of February, 1992, once again, you were at the United Nations -- the 25th of February, 1993, you were, once again, invited to attend a meeting at the UNPROFOR base in --

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: No, it was a meeting in Kiseljak at the headquarters of UNPROFOR there, and I was invited to attend the meeting which was chaired by Brigadier General Cordy-Simpson, and the meeting was attended by General Prado, I think that he was from the Spanish UN battalion, Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic was present, the chief of the main staff of the Croatian Defence Council, I was there, and the topic of the meeting was sending humanitarian aid by parachute. This was a mission, an operation, which was a fledgling one, it had just begun, and there were discussions as to the duties of the HVO linked to that humanitarian mission. At one part of the meeting, Mr. Simpson asked why the road from Busovaca to Kiseljak, why the road was still blocked, and he directed his question at Brigadier Petkovic. Petkovic answered, "It would be a good idea for you to discuss that matter with Halilovic," and he had in mind Sefer Halilovic, the chief of the main staff of the Bosnia-Herzegovina army. Petkovic indicated that Busovaca had been blocked for 32 days and that without humanitarian aid, the convoy of the BH army for the Bosniak Muslims, that they were passing via the territory of Busovaca on their way to Zenica and further on towards Tuzla, and Petkovic also emphasised that the people of Busovaca were hungry but had to let the convoys pass through. Cordy-Simpson answered Brigadier Petkovic and said that it would be a good idea for Brigadier Petkovic to contact the representatives of the UNHCR who were supplying humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When mentioning General Petkovic, he appeared at different places at meetings with you. How was he transported from Mostar? In what way did he get there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: It was only under UN organisation, and on this occasion too, I know that the Spanish battalion from Mostar, with its two combat vehicles, had brought General Petkovic to Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 27th of February, 1993, the Muslims forbade the Croats to enter certain villages. Can you say a few words about that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were the villages of the Kiseljak municipality, the Lepenica local community, and we spoke at some length about that when we discussed the conflict in Duhri. I am pointing to the village of Bukovica (indicating), the village of Zabrdje (indicating). In Bukovica, a checkpoint was set up, and there was no entry to Croats to the region of these villages, Zabrdje, Bukovica, Koscan, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. On that day, there were talks with the representative of the HVO for information in Kiseljak about radio terms.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: I asked a representative of the HVO to talk to the municipal ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: There seems to be some problem with the interpretation. Let me repeat: You had contacts with the officer in charge of information within the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please explain to us what you tried to achieve on the basis of those talks?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: Well, I told this information officer to contact the municipal civilian officers of the Kiseljak municipality to find ways and means of obtaining time on the airwaves for the members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina from the Kiseljak area who could address, via the local radio, the Bosniak Muslims in the Kiseljak municipality, to address them on the radio, because tensions in the municipality of Kiseljak were still increasing, and I wanted to calm the situation in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the same day at 10.00 with the European Monitors and with Merdan, you had talks and received information about the burning of houses.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had a meeting on the 28th of February, 1993 at 10.00, and Merdan, himself, said that the road from Busovaca to Kiseljak at the Kacuni-Bilalovac region had been blocked and that they had seen, in coming to the meeting, that houses were being set on fire, Croatian houses in Bilalovac and Kacuni. Dzemo stressed at the meeting that the barricades were of a political nature and that they were the consequence of different political decisions by the government of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and the government of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which were in contradiction to each other. At that meeting, Mr. Nakic made a report and stated that the barricades had also been set up in Vitez and that, in Novi Travnik, it was not possible to hold a meeting of the joint commission and the local commission for Novi Travnik with the representatives of the HVO and the BH army because the representatives of the BH army did not wish to come to the meeting, although Dzemo Merdan had sent an invitation to the representatives of the BH army to respond and to come to the meeting in Novi Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On that day, you received information on the release of the well-known criminal in Vitez who, once again, through use of force and violence was liberated?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I received information that Ferad Gazibaric or Gucanin had been freed from the district military prison in Busovaca, that he had been freed by an attack launched on the police and the headquarters of the military police and the military district court as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We have completed February, so, without wishing to start on March now, we can do this tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. We're going to adjourn the meeting. I should like to remind you that on Wednesdays we begin at 1.30, 1.30 p.m., and we shall be ending at 5.30. The hearing is adjourned, to be resumed tomorrow at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
